report_name: UNM Health Cyberattack Disrupts Patient Care, Extortion Group Claims Data Theft

threat_actors.name: BYOD
threat_actors.description: A newly emerged cyber extortion group that claimed responsibility for the October 2026 cyberattack against the University of New Mexico Health System. The group alleged it compromised 36,000 systems and exfiltrated large volumes of sensitive data, including patient health information (PHI), Social Security numbers, and university research.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Assessed as a likely initial access vector used by the threat actors to gain entry into the UNM Health network.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Assessed as a likely initial access vector, where attackers could have exploited an unpatched, internet-facing system to compromise the UNM Health network.

attack_patterns.name: Process Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Assessed as a likely technique used by attackers after gaining initial access to perform network reconnaissance and identify high-value targets like EHR databases and file servers.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The BYOD group claimed to have stolen vast amounts of data, including patient records and research, which would have been exfiltrated over a command and control channel.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The attack methodology, including the disruptive payload and synthetic voice message, was consistent with modern ransomware operations that encrypt data for impact to pressure victims into paying.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: Hunting hints provided in the report suggested searching for suspicious execution of `powershell.exe`, `cmd.exe`, or `wscript.exe` originating from non-standard parent processes.

attack_patterns.name: Brute Force
attack_patterns.description: Hunting hints provided in the report suggested searching for spikes in Windows Security Log Event ID 4625 (An account failed to log on) to detect potential brute-force attempts.

attack_patterns.name: Masquerading
attack_patterns.description: Hunting hints provided in the report suggested looking for the creation of files with double extensions (e.g., document.pdf.exe) as a potential indicator of related activity.

identities.name: University of New Mexico Health System
identities.description: A major US healthcare and university system that suffered a significant cyberattack in October 2026, leading to the disruption of clinical operations, diversion of ambulances, and cancellation of surgeries. The attackers claimed to have stolen patient, student, and employee data.

identities.name: Cerner
identities.description: An EHR provider whose systems were allegedly compromised during the UNM Health cyberattack, with attackers claiming to have stolen data from Cerner EHR rosters.

identities.name: Oracle
identities.description: A technology vendor whose database systems were allegedly compromised during the UNM Health cyberattack.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: A technology vendor whose Entra systems were allegedly compromised during the UNM Health cyberattack.

infrastructure.name: BYOD Data Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A data leak site where the BYOD extortion group published its claims of responsibility and data theft from the UNM Health system.

indicators.name: Suspicious Process Execution from Non-Standard Parent
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Process Execution from Non-Standard Parent
id: 9c5e8d3f-1a2b-4c3d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious script interpreters (powershell, cmd, wscript) being launched by non-standard parent processes like Office applications or browsers, as suggested in the UNM Health attack analysis.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/unm-health-ransomware-attack-disrupts-patient-care-surgeries/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-28
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\winword.exe'
      - '\excel.exe'
      - '\powerpnt.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\msaccess.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects suspicious script interpreters (powershell, cmd, wscript) being launched by non-standard parent processes like Office applications or browsers, as suggested as a hunting hint in the UNM Health attack analysis.

indicators.name: File Creation with Double Extension
indicators.pattern:
title: File Creation with Double Extension
id: 8b4d7c2e-0987-4a5b-9c8d-f1e2d3c4b5a6
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of files with a double extension, a common technique for masquerading malicious executables, as suggested as a hunting hint in the UNM Health attack analysis.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/unm-health-ransomware-attack-disrupts-patient-care-surgeries/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-28
tags:
  - attack.t1036
  - attack.t1036.007
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|re: '.*\.(pdf|doc|docx|xls|xlsx|ppt|pptx|jpg|png|txt|rtf)\.(exe|bat|vbs|scr|ps1|js)$'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of files with a double extension, a common technique for masquerading malicious executables, as suggested as a hunting hint in the UNM Health attack analysis.
